Subject: Quick follow-up after today's demo - long patient notes use case

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful overview. Two quick items from our side after the call:

1) Context window fit: our clinical summarization workload typically sends ~40–60k tokens per patient (concatenated visits, notes, labs). We heard reference to "long" model variants; can you confirm which models you'd recommend for fidelity (especially for compressive summaries) and what truncation/rolling-window behavior we'd expect?

2) Eval artifacts: can you share an initial eval pack (prompt sets + benchmark results) we can run on our side? We want to check for hallucination rate on medications and named entities and summarization fidelity at different sequence lengths.

If possible, can we get a short action plan and timeline? We're evaluating a pilot for Q3 and need to include this in our vendor short-list.

Appreciate it — Dana

Dana Park
Director of Applied NLP, AtlasAI Health

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after today's demo - long patient notes use case

Hi Dana (and Tom),

Great to connect — appreciate the concise asks. Below is a proposed plan and the materials we attached for your initial review. High-level answers first, then concrete next steps.

Short answers
- Model recommendations: rw-infer-13b-long-v2 (best cost/latency for ~32k tokens), rw-infer-70b-long (higher fidelity, better entity preservation for full 60k). Both are long-window variants with KV-cache/segmented attention optimizations.
- Truncation behavior: default server behavior preserves the most recent tokens and will evict oldest KV entries once sequence limit is reached. We recommend automated rolling-window + prefix caching for patient-history prompts (we include a reference config).
- Summarization fidelity: our internal long-context eval suite measures entity F1, hallucination rate (precision on asserted facts), and compression-ROUGE. Attached report includes a baseline on clinical-style documents.

Attachments included
- rw_longcontext_eval_report.pdf (summary of runs on clinical-ish dataset; includes entity F1 at different lengths)
- prompt_sets_v1.csv (candidate prompts including system/prompt engineering for extractive + compressive summaries)
- demo_recording_20260409.mp4 (recording of our product demo)

Proposed action plan (timeline)
- 1 business day: you review attachments; flag 3–5 representative patient notes to include in your smoke tests.
- 3 business days: we provide a HubSpot sandbox eval bundle (preconfigured prompt sets + benchmark harness) you can run in your environment or in our private preview.
- 7–10 business days: if you accept, we run a short-run pilot (sample ~1k patients) on rw-infer-13b-long-v2 and rw-infer-70b-long, produce comparative metrics and sample summaries.

Ask from you now
- Please confirm if we should send the sandbox to your security contact or directly to your engineering team. Also, any regulatory constraints (e.g., specific PII handling) we should be aware of before we share the full bundle.

I'll loop Marcus (SE) and Laura (CS) to help scope the pilot and the eval harness.

Best,

Thanks Neha & Dana — quick technical clarifications from our side to make the pilot higher signal: 

1) Input strategy: for 40–60k token records we typically recommend segmenting into visit-level chunks with a 1–2k token overlap window and a 1–2 paragraph summary prefix per chunk. That preserves cross-visit coreference while keeping per-request latency predictable.

2) Baseline prompts: I tweaked prompt_sets_v1.csv — see column "pilot_recommendation" in the attached. For entity checks, include medication, allergy, and diagnosis spans as separate assertions in the harness.

3) Regression guardrails: during pilot we propose a small continuous evaluation job that checks entity F1, hallucination precision, and a human-in-the-loop sample of 50 patient summaries/day. If we see >3% drop in entity precision vs baseline we trigger rollback to the previous model variant.

4) Access: we can provision a private sandbox (VPC) trial for AtlasAI Health if you want to run within your network — just confirm the security contact and expected timeframe.

I've attached a short config snippet for rolling-window behavior (named rolling_window_config.json) inside the Drive folder — let me know if you want that pasted into the thread.

-Marcus
